summary: Duels at sea inside the match room. Protocol v5: Buttons.Grapple (J, latched like E), duel-ready message, 'cancelled' end reason. New apps/server/src/duelMachine.ts (DuelMachine: seats and gates, countdown with probes and input delay, DuelAuthority bundles, reconnection bookkeeping, forfeits at frame boundaries) now runs both DuelRoom (start on countdown; behaviour, messages and tests unchanged) and MatchRoom (start when the rules say so; a countdown that ends early waits in 'waiting' without probes). MatchRoom builds each world tick's snapshot for stepEncounters and applies its events: stop ships, open or start or end duels, return and respawn ships. It reports end+settled on the same tick. Views filter the new grapples/markers/status/duels maps. Reserved and respawning ships are hidden; a fighter who drops keeps the seat for 10 s. Simulation: GRAPPLE_BUTTON, stopShip, returnShip, pointInSight. Web: DuelClient over a DuelTransport seam (duelRoomTransport, SeaDuelRouter); one Phaser game per page (MatchGame: sea + arena scenes); telegraphs, incoming-grapple warning, duel markers with elapsed time, protection ring; HUD lines for grapple/cooldown, warning, protection and respawn. Test tools: HeadlessDuelClient runs over either room; HeadlessClient.fighter. Tests: web/simulation/server/protocol unit tests; integration seaDuel.test.ts (15 concurrent: grapple, escape by range and by aim, no target, protected target, KO, watcher/stranger visibility incl. raw frames, return and respawn, drop/reconnect, 10 s forfeit, quit, both absent, ready forfeit/cancel/late ready) and seaDuelHarness.test.ts (80/20/1%: 181/181 hash checks, 0 desyncs; draw return); e2e seaDuel.spec.ts [scenario:sea-duel]. Harness scripts moved to tests/integration/harness.ts. Docs: architecture.md, duel.md, encounters.md, README. Checks run here: npm ci; npm run typecheck (pass); npm run test:unit (855 pass); npm run test:integration (55 pass, 200 s); npm run build (pass, smoke passed); playwright all 4 spec files with the JSON reporter (7/7 pass), and check-report said the report follows the verifier's rules.
open_assumptions: No player starts with §2 departure protection: private matches have no start of play yet, so createEncounterState gets no spawnProtected ids.

With no rubbings yet, the room sends the end and the settled report on the same world tick (decisions.md). A settled duel's lobby stays in the fighters' views for 2 s (DUEL_RESULT_TICKS) so both can read the result. The winner's protection and the loser's respawn count during it.

Fighters and players waiting to respawn see no other ship, telegraph or marker. A grapple telegraph names its target's id to observers who see the attacker. Duel markers use an opaque key and carry no player ids.
The match page's single Phaser game stays Phaser.AUTO (WebGL where available) with the arena scene inside it. The standalone duel page keeps its canvas-renderer arena game.
A sea duel's HUD 'Duel code' field shows the match code. The dev-only ?rtt=&jitter= latency setting still applies only to standalone duel rooms.
untested: A browser fighter who drops and reconnects mid-duel at sea (covered only with headless clients through the impairment proxy).
A browser whose arena loads after the 3 s countdown (the 'waiting' pause and session restart are covered only headless).
Arena frame rate and input feel inside the WebGL match game on a GPU-less machine, beyond the sea-duel scenario passing.
More than one simultaneous duel at sea in one match, and the four-duel cap, through the room (covered only by the pure encounter rules' tests).
verify_yourself: Play a sea duel in two real browsers with `npm run dev`: check that the arena inside the match's WebGL game feels as responsive as the standalone canvas arena, and that the one-second telegraph and warning are readable in time to escape.
